summary: Serverless Supabase on Azure Static Web Apps with PostgreSQL as the database; front end: React + Vite, Progressive Web App.

frontend.justification: Web: A client-rendered app behind login needs no server rendering. Fit for this project: strong cost for React + Vite (priority 3); strong performance for React + Vite (priority 5); well suited to gaming projects; strong time to market for React + Vite (priority 4). Mobile: Reuses the web app, installable without an app store. Fit for this project: strong time to market for Progressive Web App (priority 4); reuses the web codebase; strong cost for Progressive Web App (priority 3); strong maintainability for Progressive Web App (priority 3).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 0.4 points lower: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to gaming projects).
Scored 0.8 points lower: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on project.platforms (reuses the web codebase).

tradeoffs: Client-rendered: no SEO for public pages.
The team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript.
iOS limits background sync and push; browsers may evict offline storage.
Weaker camera/GPS/background-upload control than a native app.

backend.choice: Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage + Realtime + Edge Functions)
backend.justification: One managed Postgres project gives auth, storage, realtime and APIs. Fit for this project: native WebSocket/real-time support; strong time to market for Supabase (priority 4); a 3-person team ships in 10 weeks without building auth/storage; strong performance for Supabase (priority 5).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 1.7 points lower: per-request overhead is tight for p95=150ms.
Scored 1.3 points lower: the team would have to learn C#; the chosen option wins on timeline.mvp_weeks (a 3-person team ships in 10 weeks without building auth/storage).

tradeoffs: Business logic split across RLS policies, SQL and Edge Functions is harder to test.
Free projects pause after a week of inactivity; production needs the Pro plan.
The team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript.

database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: strong maintainability for PostgreSQL (priority 3); strong performance for PostgreSQL (priority 5); strong security for PostgreSQL (priority 3); strong time to market for PostgreSQL (priority 4).

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for MySQL – Flexible Server (East US)
alternatives.why_not: Scored 2.0 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.maintainability (strong maintainability for PostgreSQL (priority 3)).
Scored 2.7 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.maintainability (strong maintainability for PostgreSQL (priority 3)).

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.justification: Static hosting with Entra auth on Azure. Fit for this project: strong time to market for Azure Static Web Apps (priority 4); scales automatically with spiky traffic; strong cost for Azure Static Web Apps (priority 3); strong performance for Azure Static Web Apps (priority 5).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 0.3 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.cost (strong cost for Azure Static Web Apps (priority 3)).
Scored 0.4 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.cost (strong cost for Azure Static Web Apps (priority 3)).

supporting.justification: Included in the Supabase project; issues JWTs that Postgres RLS policies check.

alternatives.why_not: Separate vendor; user data stored in the US.

tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: Included; pushes chat messages and job-status changes to subscribed clients.
tradeoffs: Long-lived connections need sticky sessions or a pub/sub layer.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (payment webhooks, notifications, image processing, scoring) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.justification: Free push delivery to Android for job updates and reminders.

alternatives.why_not: Costs per message and DLT templates.

tradeoffs: Notification payloads must not contain sensitive data.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.

supporting.choice: Azure Monitor + Application Insights + OpenTelemetry tracing
supporting.justification: Logs, metrics and traces stay in the same cloud and region as the data.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L3: ~80000 users, ~4000 peak concurrent, ~800 req/s at peak, ~156.2 GB stored
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees, SMS and payment-gateway transaction fees
